Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident validation — zero customer-record reads (follow-up)

Hi Julia,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our focused post-incident checks. Per your request, we ran targeted access scans across the runtime workspace and KV caches for the 02/20 incident window.

High level summary: we found zero reads of Acme Payments customer records during the impacted window. We performed both pattern-matching queries against read logs and a direct hash reconciliation on relevant KV entries.

I am attaching the initial scan CSV and the low-level hash list for your security team to review. Ben is copied with technical details if you want a quick walkthrough on the checks.

Next steps we propose:
- Ben to send the scan methodology and reproducible commands (done below).
- We can schedule a short call with your security team to walk the artifacts (if helpful).
- Final signed confirmation to follow after we include sanitized log excerpts and our chain-of-custody note (ETA tomorrow).

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Julia Chen <julia.chen@acme-payments.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 13:40:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-incident validation — zero customer-record reads (follow-up)

Stephanie / Julia — quick tech note for the record.

What we ran:
1) Read-log filter: scp and internal audit logs filtered by resource IDs mapped to Acme tenancy (resource.tag=acme-payments).
2) KV reconciliation: exported keys in impacted shard range (shard 17–19) and computed SHA256(key || last_modified) against baseline snapshot taken 2027-02-19T23:00Z.
3) Prefix-scan: sampled prefixes for 1,000 requests in the window and validated no downstream reads returned customer identifiable payloads.

Commands (sanitized):
- /opt/redwood/tools/logscan --start 2027-02-20T02:00Z --end 2027-02-20T06:00Z --tenant acme-payments --out access-scan-20270221.csv
- /opt/redwood/tools/kv-dump --shard 17-19 --tenant acme-payments --hashes kv-cache-hashlist.txt

Results summary: 0 rows with read events referencing customer-record keys; hash reconciliation matched baseline for all exported keys.

Notes on scope and caveats:
- These checks were limited to the runtime and managed KV layer. They do not include third-party telemetry or customer-managed storage that Acme may integrate.
- We preserved a copy of the exact exported artifacts and the commands executed in our evidence drive folder (link below).

If you'd like, I can hop on a quick call to walk the CSV layout and hash verification steps.

Ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-incident validation — zero customer-record reads (follow-up)

Thanks Stephanie and Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

1) Can you confirm what you considered a "customer-record key" for the purposes of the scan? Were PII/PI data types explicitly included?
2) Please provide the sanitized log excerpts that show the zero-read finding and a statement we can include in our internal incident report indicating chain-of-custody for the exported artifacts.
3) Is there a signed statement or acceptance we can attach to our compliance evidence bundle?

Preferably we need those artifacts before close of business PST today. If you need more time, please flag a hard ETA.

Thanks,
Julia Chen
Security Operations Manager
Acme Payments

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-incident validation — zero customer-record reads (follow-up)

Hi Julia —

Attached are the items you requested. We prioritized producing a finalized customer-facing package:
- signed-statement-acme-0222.pdf — formal confirmation signed by Redwood Security & Compliance leadership that no Acme customer records were read during the 02/20 incident window; includes scope, methodology, and chain-of-custody summary.
- sanitized-log-excerpts-0222.txt — redacted excerpts from the read/audit logs showing the filters and zero matching events; timestamps preserved for traceability.
- access-scan-20270221.csv and kv-cache-hashlist.txt (from earlier) for reproducibility.

Quick clarifications inline:
- Definition of customer-record key: keys whose namespace maps to Acme tenant and keys that store structured customer payloads (customer_id, payment_method_id, order_history indices). PII fields were included when present; our filters matched on namespace and known customer-key prefixes.
- PII handling: sanitized-log-excerpts have all payloads redacted; when we say "zero reads of customer records" we refer to reads that returned or attempted to access payload-bearing keys mapped to Acme tenancy.
- Chain-of-custody: all exported artifacts were written to a locked evidence bucket with immutable retention, checksummed (SHA256), and we recorded the operator identities that executed the exports. Hashes are included in kv-cache-hashlist.txt.

If this is sufficient, we will send the signed PDF to your compliance mailbox and close the follow-up. If Acme wants a recorded walk-through, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
